speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual presentation; can you tell me specifically where the shooting pain originates, and does it happen more on one side or both? Have you noticed any discharge, hearing changes, or dizziness since the procedure?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the pain triggered by eating suggests nerve involvement. Have you noticed any facial weakness, numbness around the ear, or a rash in the distribution of the ear? REQUEST TEST: Gag_reflex_check; REQUEST TEST: VEMP_assessment.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Gag reflex intact. VEMP assessment not performed.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia. The combination of shooting ear pain triggered by swallowing or chewing (eating) in a patient with a recent tympanoplasty is highly specific to irritation of the glossopharyngeal nerve, likely due to post-surgical scarring or adhesions, rather than tuberculosis or a simple infection.
